blocks.x: Mt. Morris church hosts 'sweet and sacred' jazz

By James Stinard
HARLEM WEEKLY STAFF
The Mt. Morris Presbyterian Church resounded with music as the Sam Wooding-Rae Harrison Jazz Band poured on the jazz at a memorial benefit concert, Sunday, Oct. 19.

The concert billed as, 'Sweet and Sacred Jazz,' featured Sam Wooding and Rae Harrison along with their eleven man band. Sam Wooding, an energetic 85, wrote most of the jazz selections and conducted the entire program. His vivacious partner and wife, Rae Harrison performed the spiritual and blues songs. For starters, Rae sang, 'Precious Lord,' a gospel hymn written by Tommy Dorsey. Singing slowly, her rich voice resonated throughout the vaulted and glass-domed sanctuary. Rae nursed the words and concluded by repeating the last words of the song, 'I want to cross into heaven,' a total of twenty creative ways.

Introducing the next number, Sam said, 'Our people brought old melodies from Africa, called the blues. This next number, 'Kater Street Blues,' tells about the mean and ugly street I grew up in Philadelphia.'

Even though this is a lively song, one can sense a feeling of melancholy. From the beginning of 'Kater St. Blues,' as well as throughout most of the program, the audience responded by tapping their feet and moving in rhythm to the music, in addition to their enthusiastic applause.
This concert was held to raise funds for a stained-glass window to be dedicated in the memory of the late Rev. Arthur Eugene Adair.

'This program is a fitting tribute to Rev. Adair, who encouraged and promoted all types of music in the church,' said Mrs. Thelma Adair. 'To help the church purchase its pipe organ, Rev. Adair contributed a year of his salary.'
Rev. Adair founded Mt. Morris Presbyterian Church in 1942 and served as its pastor up until his death on Dec. 11, 1979.
Rev. Kumi Dwamena, acting pastor at Mt. Morris, said he felt encouraged by the way the community supported the concert.
